info.title: Votal Nexus API
info.description: One API for the web console, Nexus Mobile, the CLI and your own integrations. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.

token.description: Bearer token. Store securely; it is shown only once.

required.description: A second factor must be verified before the session is usable

enrollment_required.description: The org policy requires setting up MFA before continuing

recovery_codes.description: Unused recovery codes (another way to finish MFA)

managed_by.description: The directory this person is synced from (its values win on the next sync), or null

break_glass.description: An emergency owner account: exempt from lockout-prone policies, alerts on every use

manager_id.description: Their manager (approves access requests with a manager stage)

mfa.description: when_signalled: the IdP's MFA counts when it says MFA was used (amr / AuthnContext); always: every sign-in through it counts as MFA; never: Nexus MFA always applies

FederationServiceProvider.description: What to enter at the IdP

matched.description: MDM devices that are also Nexus devices (same serial number)

without_agent.description: MDM devices with no Nexus agent: deploy it from the MDM

stage.description: 0-based index of the approval stage it waits on

approvers.description: Who can decide the current stage (emails)

access.description: What they have, e.g. “admin role” or “via group Finance”

choices.description: Three numbers; exactly one matches what the console shows

manager_id.description: Their manager, or null for none

mfa_coverage.description: Share of active users with MFA, 0..1

mfa_policy.description: Who must enroll MFA. Users without a factor are asked to set one up at their next sign-in.

session_ttl_hours.description: How long a sign-in lasts before re-authentication

restrict_to_verified_domains.description: Only people with emails in your verified domains can be added

owners_require_passkey.description: Owners confirm admin actions with a passkey (phishing-resistant); other methods aren't accepted for them

impact.description: What changes for people if this is applied

auto_apply.description: Whether 'Apply baseline' can fix this automatically

client_type.description: `public` for SPAs and native apps (no secret; PKCE required)

metadata_xml.description: The app's SAML metadata; fills entity_id and acs_url

attributes.description: Omit for the defaults (email, firstName, lastName, displayName, groups)

next_advance_at.description: When the current stage advances by itself, if at least one of its devices updated healthily

account.description: Admin email (Google) or tenant (Entra) the connection reads

group_filter.description: Remote group IDs to sync; empty = whole directory

scim.description: For SCIM connections: where the IdP sends changes

token.description: Shown once. Paste it into your IdP as the bearer token.

prefix.description: The start of the key, to recognize it

email.description: all | important (warnings and critical) | critical only

push.description: all | important (warnings and critical) | critical only

timezone.description: Used for quiet hours and the digest

quiet_hours.description: Hold non-critical push and email during these hours; a summary follows when they end

digest.description: Send non-critical email as one daily digest at this time

people.description: People in this organization with an email in the domain

endpoint.description: S3-compatible storage only (MinIO, Wasabi, …). Leave empty for Amazon S3.

compliance_grace_until.description: Enforced checks are failing but within their grace period until then

mdm.description: What each connected MDM (Intune, Jamf) reports about this device

enforced.description: Counts toward compliance (the policy is in enforce mode)

grace_until.description: Failing, but not counted until then

mode.description: enforce: counts toward compliance (and so conditional access); audit: reported only

grace_hours.description: How long an enforced check may fail before it counts (0 = at once)

mode.description: Start in report-only to see the impact first

post.summary: Refresh, lock, restart or wipe a device (lock, restart and wipe require recent MFA)
post.description: refresh: the agent reports now. lock: through the MDM when the device is managed by one, else the agent. restart: the agent (in 1 minute), or the MDM if the device is offline. wipe: through the MDM only, irreversible: `confirm` must be the device's hostname. A Jamf lock returns the unlock PIN, once.

post.description: Body `{token, device}`. The `NexusDevice` proof JWT carries the device's new public key in its `jwk` header.

post.summary: Report posture and inventory (called by the Nexus agent every minute)
post.description: Body `{device, posture, inventory?, update_result?}`, signed with the device key (`kid` = device ID). Returns the next check-in intervals and, when this device's rollout ring is due, a signed `update` offer.

post.summary: Stream audit events to a webhook, SIEM or storage bucket (requires recent MFA)
post.description: Webhooks get a generated signing secret, returned once. `start: last_24h` backfills the last day. S3 and GCS archives write gzipped JSON lines, one object per batch of up to 1,000 events (at least every 5 minutes), under `year=/month=/day=` prefixes. For S3 and GCS the URL comes from the bucket.

url.description: Webhook, collector or Sentinel data collection endpoint URL. Not used for S3 and GCS.

secret.description: Splunk HEC token, Datadog API key, S3 secret access key, GCS HMAC secret or Entra client secret. Webhooks: leave empty to generate one.

endpoint.description: S3-compatible storage only (MinIO, Wasabi, …). Leave empty for Amazon S3.
